title: Low Write Rate, Large History
description: A service stores 20 GB/day for five years. Throughput fits one primary, but capacity planning must include three copies plus indexes. Which conclusion follows?

options.text: Low QPS proves the data fits one node indefinitely.
options.explanation: Write rate and retained size are separate limits; a modest stream accumulates a large history.

options.text: Five years is about 36 TB raw and over 100 TB for three copies, so consider partitioning or accessible archives.
options.explanation: 20 GB × 365 × 5 is roughly 36.5 TB before indexes. Replication triples that, making retention rather than throughput the design pressure.

options.text: Three copies divide the raw capacity requirement by three.
options.explanation: Replication duplicates data; it multiplies total storage rather than reducing it.

options.text: Keep only today's 20 GB in the estimate.
options.explanation: That ignores the five-year retention requirement and would under-size persistent storage.
